report:
## Conclusion

Your view is **not supported by the best available evidence**, but the claim needs careful wording. Anti-cytokine/immunomodulatory drugs **appear to reduce average depressive-symptom scores** among people being treated for chronic inflammatory disorders. This is not yet proof that they are effective treatments for *clinical depression itself*.

A systematic review/meta-analysis of randomized trials in chronic inflammatory conditions found a statistically significant antidepressant effect of anti-cytokine therapy. Importantly, depressive symptoms were generally **secondary outcomes**, not the reason patients entered the trials. Thus, the finding is credible as an average symptom benefit, but less definitive for diagnosed major depressive disorder.  
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5794896/

A subsequent patient-level “mega-analysis” pooled 18 placebo-controlled trials across nine inflammatory disorders. Its design—standardizing individual participant data—provides stronger support that immunomodulatory drugs can improve depressive symptoms, particularly among participants with greater baseline symptoms.  
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7244402/

However, several caveats prevent a stronger conclusion:

* Benefits may be **indirect**: reduced pain, fatigue, disability, or visible disease can improve mood, rather than cytokine blockade directly treating depression.
* Effects likely differ by drug, disease, and the person’s level/type of inflammation.
* Evidence does **not** justify prescribing biologics solely for ordinary depression; they have substantial costs and immune-related risks.
* In a trial of infliximab for treatment-resistant depression (not necessarily inflammatory disease), there was no generalized benefit; a possible effect was confined to people with high inflammatory biomarkers.  
https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamapsychiatry/fullarticle/1356541

So: “anti-cytokine drugs reduce depressive symptoms in people with chronic inflammatory conditions” is broadly evidence-based, whereas “they are established antidepressants” is not.
